correctness.rationale: Any two-piece hyperplane cut with both inradii ≥r contains radius-r balls in opposite half-spaces and hence with center separation ≥2r; conversely the perpendicular bisector of two nonoverlapping equal balls contained in convex C separates them into two valid inball-containing halves. For an orthotope balls are centered in R_r=∏[r,L_i−r] and can coexist iff diameter(R_r)=sqrt(∑(L_i−2r)^2)≥2r, 0≤r≤ell/2. q=B−4Ar+4(d−1)r² has derivative −4A+8(d−1)r<0 throughout admissible domain, so Δ=q(ell/2) gives exact saturated branch or unique quadratic smaller root; d-cube and rectangle specialization follow. When Δ≤0 optimal centers form diameter pair of eroded box and tangent balls enforce the unique central orthogonal-diagonal separator; Δ>0 optimum simply requires separation of two full-radius balls. These are analytic arbitrary-dimensional arguments, not inferred from finite checker.
residual_risks: Euclidean body, d≥2, L_d>0, single cut; q root must be restricted to [0,ell/2]; saturated cuts have continuum.
